nora: quick UX/SDK question: how should SDKs handle replay keys for streaming responses? e.g., when a stream cuts out mid-token and client retries, server may have partially executed side-effects.
devon: good one. proposal: streams should support an optional Resume-Token header returned by the server on partial completion. clients retry with same X-Redwood-Replay-Key + Resume-Token to indicate where to resume.
ishaan: that needs careful semantics. if Resume-Token is server-signed nonce, SDK can safely replay until that token point. otherwise we risk duplicate side-effects.
nora: agree. for onboarding sampleapps we can provide a tiny demo: server returns `Resume-Token: rt-<ts>-<sig>` after every chunk; proxy can simulate loss and force client to exercise resume flow.
devon: SDK surface: add enableAutoResume=true opt-in. Node/Python will expose hooks: onResumeNeeded(token) and a config to auto-attach replay key. Go SDK: ResumeHandler interface.
ishaan: default TTL for replay keys when paired with resume tokens should be short (1h) to avoid unbounded dedupe state. docs can recommend 24h for non-streaming idempotency flows.
ci-bot: scheduled: streaming-resume-e2e will run in nightly matrix (token-rotate, mid-stream-drop, resume-token-mismatch). posting results to #devex.
nora: i'll draft the proxy changes and sampleapp demo. devon: will update SDK proposals. ishaan: will write a short spec for token signing & TTL.
